_note: The Turn — doors distilled from the retrieved Catena Aurea (Newman tr.), verified line-by-line against ~/reception-corpus. Editorial framing AI-drafted, status:draft, pending Wilson's curation.
gravity: God gives the Ten Words at Sinai — commands meant to order a free people, not shackle them (Exodus 20); Paul, credentials in hand, counts them all as loss for the sake of knowing Christ (Philippians 3); and Jesus tells of tenants who beat, kill, and finally murder the son sent to collect fruit that was never theirs to withhold. The nerve: everything in the vineyard — the hedge, the tower, the winepress — was gift, on loan, and the tenants' whole crime is forgetting that.
trap: Becomes flat anti-Jewish caricature (indicting a whole people rather than a specific leadership's specific choice) or bare Christology-trivia (identify the stone, move on) — missing that the parable indicts anyone entrusted with a vineyard who starts treating the produce as their own.
hinge: The tenants' plan is chillingly rational — "this is the heir; let us kill him and have his inheritance" — the murder isn't rage, it's a business calculation. The horror is how reasonable it sounds from inside the wrong premise.

doors.claim: Hedge, tower, winepress — the tenants inherited an estate they didn't build, and forgot that before the first rent was ever due.

witnesses.author: Jerome
witnesses.reading: He hath 'planted' a vine of which Isaiah speaks, 'The vine of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel.' And 'hedged it round about.'

witnesses.author: Rabanus Maurus
witnesses.reading: Morally; a vineyard has been let out to each of us to dress, when the mystery of baptism was given us, to be cultivated by action.

doors.say: Nothing you're standing on was built by you — the hedge and the tower were already there before you showed up to work.
doors.do: Have them name one thing in their life or ministry they've started treating as self-made rather than received.

doors.claim: The murder is coldly reasoned — kill the heir, keep the inheritance — which is scarier than a crime of passion, because it means clear thinking got them there.

witnesses.author: Rabanus Maurus
witnesses.reading: The Jews endeavoured by putting Him to death to seize upon the inheritance, when they strove to overthrow the faith which is through Him.

witnesses.author: John Chrysostom
witnesses.reading: Wherefore then did He not send Him immediately? That from what they had done to the others they might accuse themselves.

doors.say: Sin rarely announces itself as sin — it usually shows up as the reasonable next step from a premise nobody questioned.
doors.do: Ask them to name a decision that felt perfectly rational but started from a false premise about what actually belongs to them.

doors.landing: The stone that breaks or grinds
doors.claim: There's no neutral way to meet the rejected stone — you're either broken open by it, and can be healed, or you try to grind it down and are ground to powder instead.

witnesses.author: Augustine
witnesses.reading: Those that fall upon Him, are those that despise and afflict Him. These do not perish utterly, but are broken so that they walk not upright.

witnesses.author: Pseudo-Chrysostom
witnesses.reading: It is one thing to be broken, and another to be ground to powder. Of what is broken there remains something; but what is ground to powder is as it were converted into dust.

doors.say: You cannot stay neutral toward the rejected stone — either it breaks you in a way you can recover from, or you try to break it and there's nothing left of you.
doors.do: Ask them which posture they're currently in toward something Christ has asked of them: broken open, or grinding against it.

subtract: Three landings — the forgotten gift, the cold calculation, or the two ways to meet the stone. Choose one.
source: Catena Aurea (Aquinas; J.H. Newman tr., public domain), retrieved from ~/reception-corpus — attested, not authored.

synthesis.convergence: The commandments at Sinai order a people who did not create their own freedom (Exodus 20); Paul discards every credential he actually earned to be found in Christ instead (Philippians 3); and the tenants forget, calculate, and finally kill rather than admit the vineyard was never theirs. Every reading names the same temptation: mistaking what you were given for what you made, then defending the mistake past all reason.
synthesis.claim: Whatever you're protecting as yours was on loan the whole time — the only question is whether you find that out from the owner or from a broken stone.
synthesis.here: For people or institutions confusing stewardship with ownership, don't moralize about greed in the abstract — name the specific gift they've started treating as an entitlement, and ask what rent is actually due.
